security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel stores a tagged capability to memory (e.g., during context switch, signal frame setup, KVM vCPU save/restore, or ptrace regset access) and later reloads it expecting the tag to be preserved, without re-validating the tag after the load, when the memory path traverses an MMU mapping that clears tags, a PMA region that cannot store tags, or a platform load filter that strips tags
security_spec.summary: Kernel must re-validate capability tags on every load from memory, because MMU page mappings, PMAs, and platform load filters can silently clear tags between store and load, breaking authority-preservation assumptions in context switch, signal delivery, KVM, and ptrace paths

findings.finding: This kernel (Linux 7.0-rc5, arch/riscv/) contains zero CHERI capability support. No capability registers are saved/restored in context switch paths (entry.S:421-471 __switch_to saves only integer GPRs + CSR_STATUS), no capability fields exist in thread_struct (processor.h:106-126), sigframe (signal.c:35-41, sigcontext.h:31-37), KVM vCPU context (kvm_host.h:116-154), or ptrace regsets (ptrace.c:24-38). No CHERI Kconfig option, no cheri-capable PTE handling, no revocation code. The vulnerability pattern 'capability store to memory → reload expecting tag preserved' cannot occur because the kernel never stores or reloads hardware capability tags.

spec_citations.excerpt: If pte.cap_rw=0 then: All capability loads set the loaded ctag to zero; All capability stores with the to-be-stored ctag set raise a cheri_excep_name_pte_st. If pte.cap_rw=1 then: All capability loads and capability stores operate as normal.

Non-ctag-aware busses: Writes to tagged memory will set the ctag to zero of any YLEN-aligned YLEN-wide memory location where any byte matches the memory write. The fundamental rule: the ctag and data are always accessed atomically.

Three CHERI PMA levels: Tagged memory supporting ctags; Tag Strip (load zero ctag, ignore stored ctag); Tag Fault (load zero ctag, Store/AMO Access Fault on ctag). Memory regions without CHERI ctag PMA do not require storage for ctags.
